flashcards.back_definition: Dividing a network into zones with limited, controlled connections between them, so a breach in one zone cannot easily reach the others.
flashcards.back_example: Point-of-sale terminals on their own segment that only talks to the payment server.
flashcards.back_confusion: Segmentation limits the blast radius; it does not stop the first compromise.

flashcards.back_definition: A virtual LAN: a logical broadcast domain created on a switch, so groups of ports are separated without separate hardware.
flashcards.back_example: VLAN 10 for staff, VLAN 20 for guests, VLAN 99 for management, all on the same switch.
flashcards.back_confusion: A VLAN is logical separation on shared hardware; an air gap is physical separation.

flashcards.back_definition: An access port belongs to one VLAN and connects an end device. A trunk carries tagged traffic for many VLANs (802.1Q) between switches and routers.
flashcards.back_example: Desk PCs plug into access ports; the uplink to the core switch is a trunk.
flashcards.back_confusion: Leaving user ports set to auto-negotiate trunking invites VLAN hopping.
flashcards.back_hook: Access = one lane; trunk = the motorway.

flashcards.back_definition: The firewall or router rules at the point where traffic is routed between VLANs. If those rules allow everything, the VLANs separate nothing.
flashcards.back_example: Rule: guest VLAN may reach the internet but nothing on 10.0.0.0/8.
flashcards.back_confusion: VLANs stop direct layer 2 traffic; policy at layer 3 is what controls crossing.
flashcards.back_hook: The wall needs a guarded door.

flashcards.back_definition: An attacker hopping from the first compromised machine to others inside the network to reach valuable systems.
flashcards.back_example: From a phished laptop to a file server to the domain controller.
flashcards.back_confusion: Segmentation, least privilege and monitoring east-west traffic all slow it.
flashcards.back_hook: Get in anywhere, then move sideways.

flashcards.front: Why must the management VLAN be isolated?
flashcards.back_definition: It carries access to switch, router and firewall admin interfaces. A user device there could attack the network gear itself.
flashcards.back_example: Only admin workstations on VLAN 99 can reach the switches' SSH.
flashcards.back_confusion: Putting users on the management VLAN "for convenience" undoes the segmentation.

flashcards.back_definition: Sending traffic into a VLAN the attacker should not reach, by tricking a port into trunking (switch spoofing) or using double 802.1Q tags.
flashcards.back_example: An attacker's laptop negotiates a trunk with a switch port left on auto.
flashcards.back_confusion: Fix it by setting user ports to access mode, disabling DTP and not using the native VLAN for users.
flashcards.back_hook: Jump the fence by pretending to be the gate.

flashcards.back_definition: Never trust a user or device because of where it sits on the network; verify identity, device health and permission on every request.
flashcards.back_example: A laptop on the office network still needs MFA and a healthy device check to open the HR app.
flashcards.back_confusion: Zero Trust is a technical posture, not distrust of employees.

flashcards.front: What is implicit trust, and why is it risky?
flashcards.back_definition: Trusting a device or user because it is inside the network or already logged in once. One compromised device then reaches everything.
flashcards.back_example: A flat office network where any PC can open any server's file shares.
flashcards.back_confusion: VLANs alone still leave implicit trust inside each VLAN.
flashcards.back_hook: Inside is not the same as safe.

flashcards.back_definition: Fine-grained rules around individual workloads or applications, so each one can only talk to the specific systems it needs.
flashcards.back_example: The web server may reach the app server on 8443; nothing else may reach the app server.
flashcards.back_confusion: Ordinary segmentation separates zones; microsegmentation separates individual workloads.
flashcards.back_hook: A wall around every room, not just every floor.

flashcards.front: What does a private VLAN isolated port do?
flashcards.back_definition: It can talk only to the promiscuous port (usually the gateway), not to other hosts in the same VLAN.
flashcards.back_example: Hotel rooms on one VLAN can reach the internet but not each other's laptops.
flashcards.back_confusion: Community ports can talk to each other and the gateway; isolated ports only to the gateway.
flashcards.back_hook: Everyone talks to the front desk, nobody to the neighbours.

flashcards.front: How did weak segmentation hurt Target in 2013?
flashcards.back_definition: Attackers entered through an HVAC contractor's access and reached point-of-sale systems, which should have been walled off from vendor access.
flashcards.back_example: About 40 million card numbers were stolen from the payment terminals.
flashcards.back_confusion: The firewall existed; the problem was what the rules allowed between zones.
flashcards.back_hook: The air-conditioning vendor should never see the tills.

flashcards.front: Why did Colonial Pipeline shut down operations in 2021?
flashcards.back_definition: Ransomware hit the business IT network, and without clear separation from the pipeline's operational technology, the company stopped the pipeline as a precaution.
flashcards.back_example: Fuel shortages followed along the US East Coast for several days.
flashcards.back_confusion: The attack did not touch the pipeline controls directly; uncertainty about the boundary forced the shutdown.
flashcards.back_hook: If you can't prove the wall holds, you close the gate.
